title: All checks and captures

card.idea: When you cannot see what to do, make a list: every check you can give and every capture you can make. Then make the same list for your opponent. It is short, it takes a minute, and it finds nearly everything.
card.habit: List every check and every capture — theirs before yours.

explain.text: Captures first. White can take on e5, on e6 and on g5. That is the whole list, and it took four seconds to make. Now weigh them instead of guessing.
Now checks. The rook can check on c3 and the bishop on c2. A check forces an answer, so a check is worth looking at even when it looks pointless.
Two checks here: Bh6 and Rxf5. Bh6 is answered by the knight on g8 taking the bishop. Rxf5 takes the queen. Listing them is not the skill. Comparing them is.

challenges.prompt: Tap every black piece White can capture right now.

hints.text: Three of them. Two white pieces can reach one of the three.
hints.text2: The knight on f3 has two of the captures on its own.

challenges.prompt: Tap every square White can move to and give check.

hints.text: The black king sits on b3. Which white pieces can reach a square next to it or in line with it?
hints.text2: Two squares, both on the c-file.

challenges.prompt: You have listed your own checks and captures. What goes on the list next?
options: Every check and capture your opponent has
Every square your queen could reach in two moves
How many pieces each side has left

challenges.prompt: The bishop checks on h6. Is that safe?
reasons: The knight on g8 takes the bishop on h6.
The rook on d5 defends h6.
The king on f8 takes the bishop on h6.

challenges.prompt: Same position. Play the other check.
challenges.reason: The rook takes the queen on f5 with check, and nothing on the board can take back.

challenges.prompt: One of your moves is a check and a capture at once. Find it.
challenges.reason: The rook on g7 takes the queen on f7 and checks the king on f3 down the file, all in one move.

challenges.prompt: Checkmate in one move. Find it and play it.
challenges.reason: The king on h5 has no square to run to, so a check that he cannot answer is mate. The queen on c3 can reach h3.

takeaway: List every check and every capture, theirs first, then pick.
